messages:
priya: quick follow-up re: the connector backpressure thresholds from RFC-2025-07 — we hit a weird behavior in staging where tenants started flipping to relay at ~60% cpu instead of the configured 75%
neil: hmm, timeline? did this happen during the canary cutover?
sam: saw it ~08:12 during the canary where we bumped parallelism. logs show connector liveness probes failing briefly then the ctlplane marked tenant as degraded.
maria: what metric exactly triggered the routing change? `connector.cpu` or the derived `egress.saturation`?
priya: looks like `egress.saturation` threshold had a wrong unit in the rollout config — percent vs fraction. config had `0.75` but our checker expected `75`. 🤦‍♀️
aj: oof. that's a classic. Where did that live — operator config map?
priya: yep, `tenant-router-config` in the operator helm values. I pushed a fix to the staging overlay and rolled the operator back to previous release while we confirm.
neil: two asks: 1) add a schema validation on reconcile so `0.75` vs `75` can't slip, 2) adjust canary ramp so fallback to relay doesn't happen while probes are still stabilizing (10m warm window)
sam: +1 to schema validation. also suggest we add a grace period after operator restart before evaluating per-tenant routing decisions — gives KV cache a chance to warm.
maria: agree. Grafana alert we saw was `tenant-routing-flap` — maybe lower severity during canary.
priya: proposed plan: patch operator to reject ambiguous percentage formats, add a `warm_window_ms` default = 600000, and cut canary ramp from 5% -> 50% over 30m instead of 10m. roll via feature-flagged rollout.
aj: for rollback playbook, add step to force-route tenants to `dedicated-relay` via API: `POST /admin/v1/tenant/{id}/route?force=relay` — handy for emergency cutovers.
infra-bot: deploy job started: `operator/staging v2.14.1 -> v2.14.2` (sha: abcd1234)
neil: we'll also add a test in the e2e harness that simulates short-lived probe failures and ensures no immediate tenant routing changes. keeps the guardrails tight.
priya: thanks — I'll open the PRs: schema validator + warm window + updated canary. tagging @sam @neil for review.
sam: quick question — does this affect private endpoints vs peering decisions? i.e., will the threshold flip route tenants from privatelink to relay prematurely?
priya: yes, in our routing policy we consider endpoint-health first, then capacity. if endpoint health is transient-failing, that combined with misinterpreted saturation triggered the switch. with the warm window and conservative canary we should avoid premature privatelink->relay flips.
maria: can we add an audit log entry when routing changes due to config parsing errors? helps postmortem.
priya: good call. I'll log `routing_change_cause=config_parse` when that branch triggers.
aj: timeline for prod? want to coordinate with oncall so we don't overlap any tenant migrations
priya: target next Tuesday 02:00 UTC for prod cutover, but will do a dry-run in staging tomorrow with the new schema and warm window. I'll ping oncall once staging dry-run looks clean.
neil: thanks — add a short runbook section in the PR template so reviewers see the rollback steps + metrics to watch (`egress.saturation`, `endpoint.health`, `routing_flap_rate`).
priya: will do. closing loop here — thanks y'all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy job succeeded: `operator/staging v2.14.2` (sha: abcd1234)
